$Comment: The Mastery Trainer's conversation: a short menu with three choices - see the quests they
offer (the shared quest list, opened AT the trainer so their own quests can be accepted and
handed in there), open the mastery menu, or leave.
Start.First holds the introduction, the one beat that outranks anything about quests: while the
player is carrying the quest that sent them here, pressing F opens a line written for a first
meeting instead of the standing menu. Its option carries the MarkTalked beat, which is what
credits a talk step - pressing F alone credits nothing - and then drops into the same menu
everybody else gets. Once the quest is done the line retires itself and the menu leads again.
Start.Quests routes a finished quest ahead of the menu: a player returning with a completed
mastery quest is greeted with its own line first, via the shared ready_generic screen, exactly
the way the Adventurer's Guide handles theirs. A quest row points at a screen rather than a bare
true so pressing F always shows a line before routing anywhere; ready_generic is the one every
quest here shares, since none of them need a dedicated line of their own. The four ids listed
are this pack's own mastery quests; add a row here when you add a quest that names the trainer
as its giver, so its hand-in gets the same treatment.
The Header line mirrors the player's tracked objective at the top of the conversation.
To reword any line, override the dialogue.mmo_mastery_trainer.* keys in a language file.
Name: Mmo_Mastery_Trainer
